name: Darin Balaban
statement:
My work is abstract, rooted in graffiti and movement: sweeping interlocking forms and saturated color, composed the way a jazz musician improvises — a structure strong enough to hold together at a distance, with enough life in it to reward the people who see it every day.

That second part matters most indoors. A wall in a public market is not passed once on a highway; it is lived with — by vendors setting up at dawn, families eating lunch under it, audiences facing a stage in front of it. I build paintings for that kind of daily company: energetic without being loud, colorful without tiring, detailed enough that regulars keep finding something new.

Over more than a decade I have painted large-scale work across the country — exterior walls, commercial interiors, and festival pieces, including live painting in front of crowds. I work primarily in spray paint and acrylic, I plan carefully around the permanent features of a space, and I welcome collaboration with the people who will live with the result.
